title: The colors of 1920s posters and advertisements
text: Most area: Light Ivory (6.0%), Tan (3.9%), Grey Beige (3.1%), Olive-Buff (3.0%), Blackish Brown (2.4%).

title: The colors of posters and advertisements, 1890-1909
text: Most area: Light Ivory (6.1%), Tan (5.1%), Camel (3.2%), Olive-Buff (2.6%), Pale flesh (2.2%).

title: The colors of wallpaper, 1900-1929
text: Most area: Olive-Buff (4.6%), Greyish White (3.9%), Putty (3.5%), Lion (3.4%), Ecru (3.2%).

title: The colors of textiles, 1800-1849
text: Most area: Grey Beige (2.2%), Olive-Buff (2.2%), Linen grey (2.2%), Stone (2.0%), Cool grey (1.8%).

title: The colors of postage stamps, 1930-1969
text: Most area: Platinum (4.6%), Greyish White (2.3%), White (2.0%), Grey White (1.5%), Olive-Buff (1.3%).

title: Colors designers use far more than painters
text: Design (category-balanced) against the 1800-1979 paintings of the corpus, colors in >= 150 design objects: Platinum 7.3x; Silver 6.3x; Light Grey 6.1x; Bluish Grey 5.8x; Cool grey 5.5x; White 5.4x.

title: Colors painters use far more than designers
text: Dark olive brown 12.7x; Seaweed green 6.8x; Smoky Black 5.7x; Bistre 4.6x; Café Noir 3.7x; Raisin Black 3.2x. (Paintings 1800-1979, n=10018; design n=11409.)

title: Colors that show up in design before painting
text: First decade a color's share passes twice its 1800-1840 level (and holds), design vs painting: Platinum 1860s vs 1930s; Charcoal Grey 1850s vs 1910s; Greyish Black 1860s vs 1890s. Caveat: only public-domain paintings are in the corpus, and few after 1900 (n by decade in the index), so a late painting date is partly a sampling gap.

title: The most vivid, the most muted, the darkest and the lightest decade
text: Mean chroma C* (category-balanced): most vivid 1960s (25.1, n=296), most muted 1860s (12.1, n=553); mean lightness L*: darkest 1930s (52.1), lightest 1960s (62.0). Balanced across 4+ categories per decade.

title: The most saturated and most muted kinds of design
text: Mean chroma C*: Pulp magazine covers 27.8 (n=832) is the most saturated; Glass 10.9 (n=646) the most muted.

title: The most Arts and Crafts color
text: Objects by 5 Arts and Crafts names in our data (n=38: Arthur Heygate Mackmurdo, Christopher Dresser, John Henry Dearle, Walter Crane, William Morris): biggest areas Cool grey, Silver, Bluish Grey, Charcoal Grey; most distinctive vs all design: Slate Color (19.9x), Squirrel Grey (16.7x), Brown Red (16.6x), Pompeian Red (6.7x).

title: The most Art Nouveau color
text: Objects by 13 Art Nouveau names in our data (n=82: Alphonse Mucha, Edward Penfield, Emile Gallé, Eugène Grasset, Georges de Feure, Henri Privat-Livemont...): biggest areas Silver, Black, Tan, Camel; most distinctive vs all design: Black (6.0x), Platinum Grey (5.0x), Yellowish Brown (4.9x), Silver (4.3x).

title: The most Bauhaus and modernism color
text: Not enough objects by named Bauhaus and modernism makers in the open data (n=1; the minimum is 15). Most 20th-century modernist work is still in copyright, so its images are not in any open collection.

title: The most Art Deco color
text: Not enough objects by named Art Deco makers in the open data (n=1; the minimum is 15). Most 20th-century modernist work is still in copyright, so its images are not in any open collection.

title: What changed in wallpaper, 1800-1859
text: Colors over-represented in wallpaper of 1800-1859 against all wallpaper in the data: Papyrus White (1.9x), Lavender Grey (1.8x), White (1.6x).

title: What changed in wallpaper, 1860-1929
text: Colors over-represented in wallpaper of 1860-1929 against all wallpaper in the data: Light Ivory (1.8x), Beige (1.7x), Brownish Olive (1.7x).

title: What changed in textile, 1800-1859
text: Colors over-represented in textile of 1800-1859 against all textile in the data: Benzo Brown (1.7x), Ecru (1.6x), Buffy Brown (1.5x).

title: What changed in textile, 1860-1929
text: Colors over-represented in textile of 1860-1929 against all textile in the data: French Grey (1.3x).

title: The biggest one-decade color swing
text: Light Ivory went from 0.7% of design area in the 1930s to 5.5% in the 1940s (n=543 and 528, category-balanced).

title: The designer with the most signature color
text: Anonyme, imprimeur (n=12) uses Lion on 55% of the area, 98x the design average.

title: When do vivid modern colors first appear in design?
text: Share of design area in vivid palette colors (C* >= 60), by decade, as category-balanced / commercial only / paintings: 1800s 0.23/0.0/0.33; 1810s 0.24/0.0/0.23; 1820s 0.48/0.0/1.39; 1830s 0.82/0.0/0.46; 1840s 0.62/0.54/0.31; 1850s 0.77/0.12/0.23; 1860s 0.18/0.16/0.05; 1870s 0.33/0.99/0.06; 1880s 0.5/0.45/0.19; 1890s 0.59/0.66/0.24; 1900s 0.83/1.8/0.29; 1910s 0.9/2.09/0.24; 1920s 2.14/4.28/0.22; 1930s 2.85/5.8/1.45; 1940s 5.05/6.37/0.51; 1950s 6.64/6.91/-; 1960s 12.8/7.09/-; 1970s 8.49/8.61/-. Commercial design (advertising, posters, packaging, covers, stamps, products) first passes 6% vivid area in the 1940s. Commercial n=5102; the corpus has no in-copyright 1930-1979 product design, so the late decades rest on posters, stamps and covers.

title: Colors painters (in our corpus) never reach 1% with, that design does
text: 237 named colors never reach 1% of any painting palette in 23527 public-domain paintings (as photographed). 66 of them reach 5% of at least 3 design objects; earliest 10th-percentile year first: Cream (1801, n=7); Sea Blue (1810, n=5); Merlot (1812, n=7); Bishop's Purple (1812, n=8); Daphne Red (1815, n=12); Alizarine Pink (1815, n=9); Dusty Green (1825, n=6); Greenish hospital green (1830, n=7).

title: The colors of commercial design
text: Colors over-represented in commercial design (n=5102) against all other design (n=6307): Dark silver pink (2.2x, 0.8% of area), Biscuit (2.1x, 0.6% of area), Warm silver (2.1x, 1.1% of area), Mushroom (1.8x, 0.7% of area), Bistre (1.6x, 0.6% of area), Liver Brown (1.6x, 0.8% of area).

title: The colors of the world's national flags
text: Of 197 national flags (Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons files, colors as drawn there), the most common color words by nearest name: White (132), Orient Red (43), Yale Blue (41), Gold (34), Pale Turquoise (22), Yellow (20), Red (18), Cement Grey (18).
